mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2% for three consecutive months reduces discount rates applied to expected corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of future earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-increase period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months, investors anticipate a faster than expected tightening cycle, prompting a flight to quality and a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.5% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during the 30-day pre-crossing period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS employment figures followed by a decline in UNRATE unemployment suggests strengthening labor market conditions that boost equity risk appetite, driving positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% in one month and UNRATE decreases by > 0.2% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 60% of such labor cycle events (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in GDPC1 personal consumption exceeding 3% signals robust demand momentum that persists into the next 60-day horizon, supporting equity valuation expansion and positive forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative during the identified demand expansion phase (rolling mean p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO supply index falls by more than 5% in two consecutive months, it indicates production contraction that outpaces services growth, creating a supply shock that depresses S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during the identified contraction period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 3% for three months indicates a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations, producing positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not higher than the 30-day pre-trend average during the three-month UNRATE decline (rolling mean p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in FEDFUNDS and HOUST housing starts above 1.5% monthly for two months suggest dual accommodative signals that together reduce term premium and boost 20-day forward equity returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 1.5% and HOUST increases by > 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 70% of such dual-stimulus events (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-side constraint environment (as indicated by a sustained drop in RSAFS demand metrics for three months) raises uncertainty about future capacity, leading to negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by > 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during the identified supply constraint period (rolling mean p-value > 0.05).
